root_or_strongest_cause.classification: 032 combines a real in-run Livox timestamp regression with late acceptance windows after the finite non-looping source is consumed.
root_or_strongest_cause.primary_cause: Livox timestamp regression occurred inside the 032 run and triggered callback-labeled FAST-LIO loop-back. This is not merely a late observer artifact: record_preflight_stamps.py is single-threaded spin_once and captured non-monotonic Livox header stamps, while fast_lio.launch.log reports livox_pcl_cbk loop-back with the same regressed timebase.
root_or_strongest_cause.secondary_cause: After the loop-back and after the extra TF/topic probes, the official Livox probe and FAST-LIO runtime recorder sampled a later window. The 120-frame non-looping replay had completed and stayed alive with exit_after_last_frame=false, so late subscribers saw IMU continuing but no Livox frames and no new FAST-LIO output samples.

supporting_evidence.fact: Early recorder captured 40 Livox, 40 /Odometry, and 40 /cloud_registered samples, proving output existed early in 032. The same recorder marked Livox, odometry, and cloud_registered stamps non-monotonic. Livox event seq 169 stamp/timebase is 1780753267.641985316, then seq 172 regresses to 1780753265.779138726.

FAST-LIO logged callback-labeled loop-back: imu_cbk=2 and livox_pcl_cbk=1. The livox_pcl_cbk line includes point_num=16016 and timebase=1780753265779138726, matching the regressed Livox event in preflight_stamps.json.
The finite source completed non-looping replay after 120/120 frames at log time 1780753274.18846 with exit_after_last_frame=false.
The later Livox/IMU probe observed Livox=0 and IMU=750, consistent with a finite source already consumed while the IMU replay node stayed active.
The later runtime recorder observed /Odometry=0 and /cloud_registered=0, despite early recorder evidence that these topics had been publishing before the loop-back/late-window condition.
